claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength of simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi are controlled by the absence of nanoscale secondary phases.
Only moderate lattice distortion contributes to the low strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
A homogeneous CoCrFeNiTi solid solution permits relatively easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide underpins the favorable plasticity and machinability of CoCrFeNiTi while limiting its hardness and yield strength.
A controlled aging treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates or ordered domains in near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The induced nanoscale phases may occur within grains or at grain boundaries.
Nanoscale precipitates or ordered domains act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The proposed precipitates strengthen CoCrFeNiTi through an Orowan-type dislocation-pinning mechanism.
The precipitates or ordered domains enhance lattice resistance to dislocation motion.
Aged or precipitate-bearing CoCrFeNiTi should have higher yield strength and hardness than the unaged homogeneous solid solution.
The predicted strengthening should be accompanied by reduced compressive ductility.
Aged samples should show a higher load at yield onset and less plastic deformation before failure.
As-cast or homogenized equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can serve as a simple-solid-solution baseline without aging-induced secondary phases.
Between 25 and 600 °C at approximately 1 × 10^-3 s^-1, dislocation mechanics rather than diffusion or creep should dominate the proposed response.
Compression testing at 25 and 600 °C and an initial strain rate of 1 × 10^-3 s^-1 is consistent with conditions used in the cited prior studies.
In Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr, annealing produced approximately 50 nm B2 precipitates in a disordered BCC matrix and increased yield strength relative to the weakly ordered, more ductile condition.
The cited refractory alloy provides evidence for an association between ordered or precipitate-containing microstructures, increased strength, and reduced ductility.
